notes: Lead source: self-serve signup; small CS team (60 ppl) building a chat-first support UX.
Primary pain: perceived slowness in chat responses during demos to end-customers. They reported "slow" at ~0.7-1.0s on average per generated chunk from EU region tests.
Customer context: hosted API only for now; wants no infra to manage. Cost-sensitive — tight SMB ARR expectations. Wants <400ms p95 for short Q/A if possible.

What we tried: SE ran 10k synthetic requests against eu-west and us-west endpoints. eu-west median 420ms, p95 880ms; us-west median 260ms, p95 480ms. Logs: no repeated timeouts, but some long tail spikes aligned with larger prompt sizes.
Observed patterns: longer system instructions + embedding context (3-5 docs) = higher latency. Large single-turn prompts (>1.5k tokens) push higher kernel runtimes and slightly worse tail latency.
- Region choice: prefer us-west for ReplyNest beta customers (most users in NA). For EU customers, suggest eu-west but run a quick ping/latency suite from their users to confirm.

- Timeouts: set HTTP request timeout to 60s default for normal usage, but tune socket/read timeout to 12s for chat streams. For synchronous non-streaming calls, advise 30s request timeout. Provide example curl/SDK snippets.
- Streaming: enable streaming to improve perceived latency for longer responses. Stream first tokens ASAP and render progressively in the UI.
- Prompt length guidance: compress system instructions, move rarely-changing context to prefix cache or embeddings retrieval. Aim to keep prompt base under ~800 tokens for sub-400ms p95 on us-west.

- Batching/caching: recommend caching common prefixes (e.g., a templated system prompt) and avoid sending full doc content on each call; use embeddings service to fetch top-k passages then short context.
- Model selection: use smaller/high-throughput variant for high qps chat paths; prepare fallback to higher-quality model for escalation paths. Discuss quantized variants for cost-sensitive workloads.

- Retry and fallback policy: implement a short exponential backoff + route to fallback model/region when transient latency spikes occur. Redwood's routing can be configured to prefer region then fallback to compatible variants.
Customer quotes captured: 'We love the accuracy but customers notice the lag in demos' — wants pragmatic changes, not a full infra project.

Suggested POC plan (agreement on call): 1) run parallel perf tests from us-west + eu-west (2 weeks), 2) implement streaming and 30s timeout in their app, 3) reduce system prompt and test p95 change, 4) review results and propose small paid pilot if p95 < 450ms in target region.
Risks: SMB budget — likely stays hosted; not ready for Dedicated. Data residency not a blocker now but they asked about retention controls and audit logs if they scale.
